intersection.headline: Nike pairs NFL stars with designers for tunnel fashion: Ja'Marr Chase and Advisry's Keith Herron create 'Sport Luxe' look
intersection.summary: Nike's athlete-styling programme pairs NFL players with designers to create custom pregame-arrival outfits. Earlier pairings were CeeDee Lamb with Bode and Saquon Barkley with Public School New York. Chase's look reworks Nike Tech apparel with Advisry. It turns tunnel walks into a sport, fashion and brand-marketing platform.

sports.headline: Senegal reinstated as AFCON 2025 champions after CAS overturns CAF ruling
sports.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport unanimously upheld Senegal's appeal. It set aside the CAF Appeal Board decision that had awarded Morocco the title by forfeit, and restored Senegal's 1-0 win in the January final. The panel said the referee had sole authority over the match after Senegal's walk-off.

sports.headline: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers, then move to cut him after he said coach McCarthy fell asleep in meetings
sports.summary: The Steelers benched the 42-year-old quarterback late Tuesday, despite his one-year deal worth about $22.5m. After Rodgers criticised head coach Mike McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, the team was reported to be preparing to release him. This could be his final NFL season.

sports.headline: NBA assembles €10bn arena fund to support European expansion
sports.summary: Investors including Apollo, Ares and JP Morgan are backing an initiative to fund and develop arenas across Europe. The aim is to lure top clubs to the NBA's planned European league. The article URL could not be confirmed, so the link is to the SportBusiness news listing.

sports.headline: Newcastle's Saudi owner PIF to sell up to 25% of the club via new shares
sports.summary: PIF has hired JP Morgan to sell up to a quarter of Newcastle through a new share issue. The money would go into the club to fund a new stadium of around £1.3bn or a redevelopment of St James' Park, and PIF would stay the majority shareholder. The move comes as PIF scales back its sports spending.

sports.headline: NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix takes on NBA and NHL for viewers
sports.summary: Netflix streams Packers-Rams in the first NFL Thanksgiving Eve telecast, under a deal running to 2029. It goes head-to-head with an NBA tripleheader on ESPN and an NHL doubleheader on TNT. The story is a test of streaming's pull for live sport.

sports.headline: Michigan rescinds Trev Alberts' athletic director offer, faces potential $17.2m buyout
sports.summary: A source told FOS that incoming university president C. Cybele Raver made the decision to reverse course. Alberts' attorney says the full $17.2m buyout is owed and that the MOU has no contingency language.

fashion.headline: Marc Jacobs sales hit $509m in its last year under LVMH
fashion.summary: WWD reports the brand's financials for its final year under LVMH ownership. LVMH agreed to sell it to WHP Global earlier this year, with Marc Jacobs staying on as creative director.

fashion.headline: Victoria's Secret names Edgewell CEO Rod Little as next board chair
fashion.summary: The lingerie brand announced the appointment, effective after its 2027 annual meeting and subject to shareholder re-election. It is a governance change at a major US fashion retailer. The link is to FashionNetwork US, which carried the news, as no article URL was confirmed.

marketing.headline: Pangaia takes its clothes off its website for Black Friday and replaces them with tree-planting projects
marketing.summary: On 27 November the London-based materials-science brand will swap its entire online assortment for four tree-planting projects that shoppers can fund through Ecodrive. The tagline is 'This Black Friday, no more hoodies. Only trees.' It goes further than its earlier discount-for-donation approach.

marketing.headline: Vodafone installs giant hand with remote at Waterloo station to promote TV service
marketing.summary: An out-of-home stunt created for Vodafone's TV service, covered by Campaign on 24 November. The link is to the Campaign homepage, as the article URL was not confirmed.
